name: stave_cylinder
title: A smooth round column about 6 studs across, four staves of curved slopes clipped round a core with studs on all four sides.
why: A big smooth round column, rocket stage, tank, or silo 6 studs across, where round bricks are too small and a brick-built polygon too jagged.
note: The core is fixed at 4 x 4, so the section is 6.4 studs across; 8 to 12 needs wider staves (61678 4 x 1 curved slopes) and reads squarer. Side studs sit 1.75 plates up a brick, so the staves stand half a plate above the core.

name: stepped_curve_hull
title: A hull side that curves in as it rises, a contour stack of plate layers each set in from the one below, every layer's edge finished with a curved slope so the steps read as one smooth sweep.
why: A display hull's shoulder or a curved upper deck that should read as one smooth curve, not stair steps.
note: Builds only the convex half (curving in as it rises); the book's S-curve also turns vertical on side-stud bricks and hinges its upper part, which this doesn't.

name: bare_stud_greeble
title: A hull surface tiled about 70 percent smooth, with small irregular patches of bare studs and a few dark seams, so it reads as busy plating with no greebles bolted on.
why: Any big flat surface of a display ship or station, so it reads as busy plating with no bolted-on greebles.
note: VARIANT of greeble_strip: an area version, tiles and seeded bare patches on top studs instead of details on side studs.

name: porthole_band
title: A clean, smooth band along a ship's side, with a row of round portholes set flush in it.
why: A clean white band of round portholes on a ship's upper hull, above the dark lower courses.
note: VARIANT of portholes: round tiles flush in a band of tiles on side studs, instead of Technic bricks in the course.

name: saucer_petal_panels
title: A round disc 12 studs across whose top is broken into tiled panels with radial seams and a few bare patches, like the plating of a display saucer, round a small domed hub.
why: The top of a saucer or any round flat deck, panelled with radial seams and a few bare patches round a hub dome.
note: Grid-friendly fallback: four 6 x 6 plates with a round corner make the disc and radial tiling makes the petals; the book's wedge-plate petals tilted a few degrees on hinges aren't built.

name: radial_spoke_saucer
title: The frame of a big flat disc that stays rigid without a baseplate, eight spliced spokes of plates from a hub, with a lit window block at the tip of each straight spoke.
why: The rigid frame under a big flat disc (a saucer, a landing pad, a round deck) with lit window blocks at the rim.
note: Four straight spliced spokes and four stepped diagonal ones; the book's eight true radial spokes need 45 degree turns.

name: axle_round_stack
title: A thin round booster, tank, or pole, 2 x 2 round bricks threaded on a Technic axle, with dark round plates as bands and a cone for a nose.
why: Thin round boosters, tanks, masts, and poles up to 2 studs across that must stay straight.
note: The axle goes in its own step after the stack (slid down from the top before the nose). The validator accepted the axle through the round bricks' axle holes.

name: angled_display_stand
title: A low black stand that holds a model nose-up at 10 to 20 degrees on a cradle pinned to a short pylon, so the model looks in flight and lifts off.
why: Every display ship or flyer: a low black stand that shows it nose-up in flight and lets it lift off.
note: The cradle turns by any angle on a Technic axle 4 through the pylon; it's placed with a small helper that finds the footprint corner so the rail's middle hole lands on the axle, and the validator accepted the joint at 15 degrees. Simplified from the book: a plate cross with no wedge taper and no diagonal brace. The model goes in as a submodel (ship=).

name: lancet_window
title: A row of tall round-headed Gothic windows at midi scale, each a 1-wide stack of glass centered on a jumper in a 2-stud bay, lit below and dark above, between stone piers.
why: A Gothic nave or chapel wall at midi scale: rows of tall round-headed windows, lit below and dark above.
note: VARIANT of window_frame (midi): a 1-wide window centered on a jumper in a 2-stud bay.

name: rose_window_ring
title: A big round window in a flat Gothic facade, a ring plate standing on side studs with colored glass flush in its hole, over a gallery of little columns and under a gable.
why: The big round window in a Gothic west front or transept facade.
note: A 2 x 2 dish stands in for the book's printed round tile, and a gable of 45 degree slopes for its inverted arch and 1 x 6 arch, which don't make a 4-wide round frame with the parts found.

name: flying_buttress_arch
title: A row of flying buttresses at midi scale, each an arch leaping from a slim outer pier to the nave wall, its back sloped up toward the wall and a pinnacle on the pier.
why: Flying buttresses along a Gothic nave or round an apse, each with a pinnacle on its pier.
note: REPLACES flying_buttress_bar: the book leans a bar in clips at about 45 degrees; this grid version springs a 1 x 4 arch from the pier to the wall. VARIANT of buttress.

name: pinnacle_stack
title: Small pointed Gothic pinnacles, a stack of round plates under a cone and a slim spike, set in rows on buttresses and parapets so the roofline bristles.
why: Rows of small pointed pinnacles on buttress tops and parapets, the bristling roofline of a Gothic building.
note: The book's spike wasn't identified; a cone 1 x 1 with a wand in its hollow stud stands in, which the validator accepts as held.

name: pointed_buttress_strip
title: A slim stone pilaster with fine vertical ribs and a rounded head, standing a plate proud of a tower's face on side studs.
why: Slim ribbed pilasters up the corners and faces of a Gothic tower.
note: VARIANT of buttress (flat, on side studs). The head is a 1 x 1 tile with a rounded end; the book's pointed piece wasn't identified.

name: belfry_louvers
title: The slatted openings of a bell tower, a column of bricks with studs on four sides whose side studs carry cheese slopes as slats, so each opening is filled with sloping louvers.
why: The slatted openings of a bell tower or belfry, at midi scale.
note: One slat per side stud; the book fits two cheese slopes per side per brick.

name: steep_nave_roof
title: A long steep roof of 45 degree slopes built apart as a submodel, its seams staggered course to course, with double slopes along the ridge, set on the walls so it lifts off to show the inside.
why: A long steep slate roof that lifts off a nave, chapel, or hall to show its floor.
note: VARIANT of gable_roof plus lift_off_roof_seat, built apart as a submodel; no cross-gable for a transept.

name: slender_column_capital
title: Rows of thin round columns in twin pairs, each pair joined at the top by a plate and a tile that read as the capital and the springing of the vault, for the inside of a midi-scale hall or nave.
why: Rows of thin columns inside a hall or nave, carrying the vault.

name: triangle_tile_floor
title: A patterned stone floor of 2 x 2 triangular tiles in two colors, set so the triangles meet in diamonds and stars, for the floor of a hall or a cathedral at midi scale.
why: A patterned stone floor of diamonds and stars inside a hall or cathedral.
note: VARIANT of tiled_floor. The triangular tile's body is 1.85 studs square, so each turn has its own seating offset (SEAT); two fit one 2 x 2 cell with no collision.

name: banded_round_turret
title: A slim round corner turret of 2 x 2 round bricks with a dark recessed ring and a slight lip every few bricks, the string courses of a midi-scale tower.
why: Slim round corner turrets with string-course rings on a midi tower, castle, or civic building.

name: architecture_base
title: The finished display base of an architecture model, a dark stepped frame round a tiled ground strip, with a long name tile set in the front edge and bare studs only where the model and its trees stand.
why: The finished display base under any architecture or midi model: a stepped dark frame, a tiled ground, and a name tile.
note: The name tile is plain white; the sets use a printed black tile.

name: rounded_pier_nose
title: A bridge pier 4 studs wide whose ends are smooth half-rounds, quarter-round bricks round a round core, so the water parts round its nose.
why: Bridge piers, harbor walls, or any wall end that should be smoothly half-round.
note: The cap is flat (quarter-round and round tiles); the book domes the nose with curved slopes.
